Slice: Return Tool

Intent

Let a borrower bring a tool back and end their loan themselves, from My Loans. The tool is then back in the shed, for the next holder or for anyone to borrow. The return records whether it was late, which is what counts toward a neighbor being flagged.

Trigger & Actor

The borrower, from their own My Loans screen, for one of their own loans. My Loans offers Return on every loan it lists (INV-MYL-12), including overdue loans, loans whose tool was retired while out, and loans of a suspended neighbor. The shed manager does not record returns; a tool that never comes back is recorded lost instead (Record Tool Lost).

Command / Input

Command: Return Tool

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor returning, who must be the one making the request and the loan's borrower (INV-RET-1).
loanId LoanId yes The loan to end. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-RET-11), and still out (INV-RET-2).

There is no field for the tool's condition: nothing about it is recorded on return. A damaged tool is the shed manager's to retire.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Loans @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Returned → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan drops off), Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (the tool is back in the shed), Holds To Fulfill (a returned tool with holds waiting), Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices (the loan has ended), and Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors (whether the return was late, and the late return behind a flag).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
toolId ToolId yes The loan's tool, from its Tool Checked Out. Carried so views about tools and holds match on the tool directly.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool's name on the loan's Tool Checked Out.
neighborId NeighborId yes Set by the system: the borrower on the loan's Tool Checked Out (the same as the command's, by INV-RET-1). Carried so readers about neighbors match on the borrower directly.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (Tool Checked Out.dueDate, moved by any Loan Extended), the date late was judged against.
returnedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.
returnedOn Date yes Set by the system: the calendar date of returnedAt in the shed's local time zone.
late Bool yes Set by the system: yes when returnedOn is after the loan's due date in force at the moment of return (INV-RET-4).

The event never changes. returnedOn and late are worked out once, by the command's handler, so every view reads the same answer.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Returned ends the loan in My Loans, Overdue Loans To Notify and Undelivered Notices; puts the tool back in the shed on Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (or drops a tool retired while out); adds a tool with holds waiting to Holds To Fulfill; and gives Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors a late or on-time return. Each is specified in its own doc, and all are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Once a loan is returned, no overdue notice goes out for it (INV-OLN-4, Overdue Loans To Notify). A returned tool with no holds waiting is available to borrow straight away; one with holds waiting is reserved, and until Hold Fulfilled is recorded only the neighbor at the front of the queue may check it out (INV-CHK-3a, Check Out Tool). Late returns count toward a neighbor being flagged, 3 within 90 days (Neighbors To Flag). Those rules are owned by those slices.

  • INV-RET-1: The borrower returns their own loan themselves, from My Loans.
    • The request must come from the neighbor it names, and the loan must be theirs. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager does not record returns.
  • INV-RET-2: Only a loan that is still out can be returned, and only once.
    • A loan ended by the shed manager recording the tool lost can't be returned.
    • A closed account never has a loan out, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
  • INV-RET-3: Returning a tool records only Tool Returned.
    • Setting the tool aside for the first waiting hold is a separate system reaction to the return, recorded as Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold).
  • INV-RET-4: A return is late when it happens after the loan's due date: from the start of the day after the due date, in the shed's local time.
    • A return on the due date itself is on time. The due date is the one in force at the moment of return: the latest Loan Extended's dueDate, or Tool Checked Out's if never extended.
    • Tool Returned records the answer as late, with the date of return as returnedOn.
  • INV-RET-5: An overdue loan can be returned.
  • INV-RET-7: A suspended neighbor can return a tool.
  • INV-RET-9: A tool retired while on loan can still be returned.
    • The return ends the loan as usual. The tool stays retired: it doesn't come back into the Tool Catalog or Tool Inventory, and no hold is waiting on it, because retiring it ended its holds.
  • INV-RET-10: Returning a loan that this borrower has already returned succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second return.
  • INV-RET-11: The loan must have been checked out.
  • INV-RET-12: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: on-time return, no holds (INV-RET-1, INV-RET-3, INV-RET-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan L1, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it
    • When: at 15:00 on 11 October, shed time, Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1, with toolId T1, the time it was recorded, returnedOn 11 October, and late no. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Return on the due date (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 12 October, late no.
  • Late return (INV-RET-4, INV-RET-5)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana returns L1 at 00:05 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with returnedOn 13 October, late yes.
  • Return after an extension (INV-RET-4)
    • Given: L1 was due 12 October, and Loan Extended moved its due date to 19 October
    • When: Ana returns L1 on 15 October
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded with late no, judged against 19 October.
  • Return with a hold waiting (INV-RET-3)
    • Given: Ana has L1, and Ben's hold on T1 is at the front of the queue
    • When: Ana returns L1
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded. No Hold Fulfilled is recorded by this command; setting T1 aside for Ben is Fulfill Hold's.
  • Suspended neighbor returns a tool (INV-RET-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended and has L1 out
    • When: Ana returns L1 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L1.
  • Returning a tool that was retired while on loan (INV-RET-9)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder (T2) on loan L2, and Tool Retired was recorded for T2 while it was out
    • When: Ana returns L2 from My Loans
    • Then: Tool Returned is recorded for L2, with toolId T2. T2 stays retired.
  • The same return twice (INV-RET-10)
    • Given: Tool Returned was recorded for L1
    • When: Ana's same Return Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Loan already recorded lost (INV-RET-2)
    • Given: Tool Lost was recorded for Ana's loan L3
    • When: Ana asks to return L3
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded.
  • Someone else's loan (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: Ben asks, for himself, to return L1
    • Then: refused with not-your-loan: "You can only return your own loans." No event is recorded.
  • A request in someone else's name (INV-RET-1)
    • Given: Ana has L1 out
    • When: a request from Ben asks to return L1 for Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only return loans for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown loan (INV-RET-11)
    • Given: no loan has ID L9
    • When: Ana asks to return L9
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-RET-12)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for returning a tool arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the borrower on the My Loans screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-RET-12): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-RET-1).
  3. loan-not-found (INV-RET-11).
  4. not-your-loan (INV-RET-1).
  5. If Tool Returned is already recorded for the loan, the request is a repeat: it succeeds and records nothing (INV-RET-10).
  6. loan-ended, if Tool Lost is recorded for the loan (INV-RET-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-RET-12
requester-mismatch You can only return loans for yourself. INV-RET-1
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-RET-11
not-your-loan You can only return your own loans. INV-RET-1
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-RET-2

requester-mismatch and loan-not-found can only come from a faulty or impersonating caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan, and loan-ended uses the same sentence.

Suspension, an overdue loan and a retired tool never stop a return; there is no refusal for them.

Idempotency: a return is identified by its loan. A repeat after the loan was returned succeeds and records nothing. A loan ended by Tool Lost is refused, because returning it would be a different outcome from the one recorded.

Requests at the same moment: each Return Tool is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan. Of a return and a Record Tool Lost for the same loan at once, whichever is decided first is recorded; the other finds the loan ended (a return then gets loan-ended, or succeeds as a repeat if the first was itself a return).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a borrower may return only their own loans (INV-RET-1); the shed manager doesn't record returns. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Returned holds no name or email; it records which loan ended, when, and whether it was late.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (this slice): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/check-out-tool.md and slices/extend-loan.md. Record Tool Lost is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans, Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, Holds To Fulfill, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Neighbors To Flag and Neighbors. Fulfill Hold reacts to a returned tool with holds waiting.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded; Check Out Tool no longer feeds the merged Neighbors view, Return Tool does (2026-11-01)
"},{"index":3,"name":"Neighbors To Flag","x0":627.76,"x1":771.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Neighbors To Flag

Intent

The late-return flagger's to-do list: every neighbor whose late returns have reached the threshold (3 within 90 days) and who hasn't yet been flagged for them, with the loans those late returns belong to, each with the tool's name, the due date it missed and the date it came back. The flagger works through it, so the shed manager sees each of these neighbors flagged on Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Late Return Flagger, a system processor in the Flag Neighbor slice (slices/flag-neighbor.md). No person or screen reads this list.
  • What the flagger does with it: for each neighbor returned, it issues Flag Neighbor naming the loans returned, which the flag uses up.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors To Flag built from events: "Tool Returned", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the Late Return Flagger (Flag Neighbor). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events (seconds, not minutes). Which late returns are still within the 90 days is worked out when the list is read, from returnedOn and today's date in the shed's local time zone.

The view keeps one row for every late return that can still count toward a flag; the query groups them by neighbor. LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Tool Returned.neighborId: the borrower.
loanId LoanId Tool Returned.loanId.
toolName Text Tool Returned.toolName. Carried onto the flag.
dueDate Date Tool Returned.dueDate: the due date in force at the return. Carried onto the flag.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn.
inWindow Bool Derived: yes while returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before it, in the shed's local time zone (INV-NTF-2). Worked out when the list is read.

To decide whether a return creates a row, the view also keeps, beyond its rows, every neighbor's current status: active, suspended (from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated) or closed (from Neighbor Account Closed). This is bookkeeping, not rows, and is never returned.

When a row is created. Tool Returned with late = yes creates a row for the loan's borrower, unless the borrower is suspended or their account is closed (INV-NTF-6, INV-NTF-7). An on-time return creates nothing. Lateness is read from Tool Returned.late, recorded once by Return Tool; this view never works it out.

When rows are removed.

  • Neighbor Flagged removes the rows for the loans it names as used up (INV-NTF-3).
  • Neighbor Suspended and Neighbor Reinstated remove all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-5, INV-NTF-7).
  • Neighbor Account Closed removes all of the neighbor's rows (INV-NTF-6).

Nothing puts a row back.

Queries

  • List neighbors to flag. Takes nothing. Returns each neighbor who has at least 3 rows with inWindow yes, with their neighborId and those rows as late returns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn; all of them, if more than 3). There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the flagger.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NTF-1: Only late returns count toward the threshold.
    • Whether a return was late is recorded on Tool Returned (late), worked out by Return Tool against the loan's due date in force, after any extensions. A return on the due date is on time.
    • A loan that is still out doesn't count, even if it is overdue, until it is returned late.
    • A tool recorded lost never counts as a late return, even if the loan was overdue: it is never returned, so it never produces a Tool Returned.
  • INV-NTF-2: A neighbor is on the list when they have 3 or more late returns within the last 90 days that haven't counted toward a flag.
    • The 90 days are a rolling window, counted back from today by the date of each return. A late return older than that no longer counts. A late return counts on the day it was returned and the next 89 days, 90 calendar days in all, in the shed's local time. A return on 1 June counts through 29 August.
  • INV-NTF-3: Once Neighbor Flagged is recorded for a neighbor, the late returns it names are used up and never count again.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries every late return that counted when the flag was recorded. This list uses them up by loan; Neighbors shows them.
    • The neighbor leaves the list, and is flagged again only after 3 new late returns within 90 days.
    • A flag the shed manager doesn't act on stays open on Neighbors. It doesn't put the neighbor back on this list.
  • INV-NTF-5: Reinstatement starts a neighbor's late-return count again from zero.
    • Late returns from before Neighbor Reinstated never count toward a later flag.
  • INV-NTF-6: A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Account Closed is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it. An account can't be closed while tools are on loan, so no late return follows a closure.
  • INV-NTF-7: A suspended neighbor is never flagged.
    • Once Neighbor Suspended is recorded, the neighbor leaves the list if they are on it, and late returns while they are suspended aren't counted. Reinstatement then starts their count again from zero.
  • INV-NTF-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

The list has no screen; only the Late Return Flagger reads it. The shed manager sees flagged neighbors on Neighbors.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana is an active neighbor with no late returns counting, and today is 5 October.

  • On-time return doesn't count (INV-NTF-1)
    • Given: Ana's drill loan L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 on 12 October, with late = no
    • Then: no row is created, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Late return below the threshold (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has one late return counting, on 1 September
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L2 on 20 September, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has two late returns counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Third late return within 90 days (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 September (L1) and 20 September (L2)
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L3 on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3.
  • Old late return has dropped out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns on 1 June and 20 September, neither used up
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: only two of Ana's late returns are within 90 days, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Four late returns in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1, 10 and 20 September, and the flagger hasn't acted yet
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 5 October, with late = yes
    • Then: the list returns Ana with all four loans.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: the list returns Ana with L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: those rows are removed, and Ana is not on the list.
  • Flagged again only on new late returns (INV-NTF-3)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October, using up L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan L4 on 12 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, L4, and she is not on the list.
  • Reinstatement resets the count (INV-NTF-5)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has since been reinstated, and had two late returns counting before her suspension
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan on 10 October, with late = yes
    • Then: Ana has one late return counting, and she is not on the list.
  • Account closed while on the list (INV-NTF-6)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Suspended while on the list (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: the list returns Ana, waiting to be flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana's rows are removed, and the list doesn't return her.
  • Late return while suspended (INV-NTF-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for her loan, with late = yes
    • Then: no row is created.
  • Last day in the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 8 July, 20 September and 1 October; today is 5 October, which is 89 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 5 October
    • Then: all three are in the window, and the list returns Ana.
  • First day out of the window (INV-NTF-2)
    • Given: as above, but today is 6 October, 90 days after 8 July
    • When: the list is read on 6 October
    • Then: the 8 July return no longer counts, and the list doesn't return Ana.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NTF-8)
    • Given: Ana has late returns counting on 1 and 20 September
    • When: the same Tool Returned for her 20 September return is applied again
    • Then: Ana still has two late returns counting.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NTF-8).
  • The flagger reads a neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands: the list may return the same neighbor on two reads in a row. Flagging once for the same late returns is Flag Neighbor's rule, enforced when it records Neighbor Flagged; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Late Return Flagger. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds neighbor and loan IDs and return dates only. No names or emails.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, neighborId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, lateReturns (loanId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn): the late returns it uses up.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match return-tool.md. Loan Extended is no longer read here: lateness comes from Tool Returned.late.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The Late Return Flagger reads it and issues Flag Neighbor.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)
"},{"index":4,"name":"Flag Neighbor","x0":796.76,"x1":940.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Flag Neighbor

Intent

When a neighbor's late returns reach the late-return threshold, record that they crossed it, carrying the late returns behind the flag, so the shed manager sees them on Neighbors and decides whether to suspend them. The system flags; a person decides.

Trigger & Actor

Internally triggered. The Late Return Flagger, a system processor in this slice, acts whenever a neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, and issues Flag Neighbor for them with the loans that list gives. It is driven by events, not a schedule: a neighbor joins that list when a late return is recorded. No person flags a neighbor, and there is no screen. The neighbor isn't told; a flag is a prompt for the shed manager, not a penalty.

Command / Input

Command: Flag Neighbor

A NeighborId or LoanId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's flaggedAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to flag. Must be a registered account (INV-FLG-10), not closed and not suspended (INV-FLG-5).
lateReturns LateReturnFact[] yes The late returns behind the flag, as Neighbors To Flag gave them: each a loanId, toolName, dueDate and returnedOn. Must be exactly the neighbor's counting late returns today, matched by loan (INV-FLG-4), and at least 3 of them (INV-FLG-2). Order doesn't matter.

Trigger

Triggered by: processor Late Return Flagger, also in this slice, reading Neighbors To Flag.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Flagged → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (the account's open flags: count, latest flag date and the late returns behind each) and Neighbors To Flag (the named late returns are used up).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
lateReturns LateReturnFact[] yes From the command: the late returns this flag uses up, each with its loanId, toolName, dueDate and returnedOn. At least 3. Carried so Neighbors shows them without looking anything up.
flaggedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the flag date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. It carries the loans, not copies of names or dates; readers find each loan's tool and return date from its own events. A later flag records a new Neighbor Flagged.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Its processor reads Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md). Neighbor Flagged feeds Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) and takes the named late returns off Neighbors To Flag. Both are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A counting late return, for a neighbor today, is a loan of theirs whose Tool Returned has late yes, and which:

  • counts on its return day and the next 89 days: returnedOn is today or one of the 89 days before, in the shed's local time;
  • isn't named by an earlier Neighbor Flagged for them;
  • was returned after their latest Neighbor Reinstated, if any;
  • was not returned while they were suspended.

A tool recorded lost has no Tool Returned, so it never counts. Once flagged, the neighbor shows as flagged on Neighbors until the shed manager acts; there is no dismiss action (Neighbors owns how it shows). Neighbors are flagged by the system only, through the processor above.

  • INV-FLG-2: A neighbor is flagged when they have at least 3 counting late returns.
    • "At least 3" is tested on the neighbor's own counting set, worked out from their events when the command is handled, not on the loans the command names. Loans that don't count are never made up for by naming them.
  • INV-FLG-3: Flagging never suspends anyone.
    • Flag Neighbor records only Neighbor Flagged. The shed manager decides whether to suspend a flagged neighbor (Suspend Neighbor).
  • INV-FLG-4: A flag uses up the late returns that caused it.
    • Neighbor Flagged carries every counting late return the neighbor has when it is recorded, even if there are more than 3. Those loans never count again.
    • The neighbor is flagged again only after 3 new counting late returns.
  • INV-FLG-5: A neighbor is flagged only while they are still due a flag.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed is never flagged, and nor is a suspended neighbor. A neighbor whose count was reset by reinstatement after they joined Neighbors To Flag is not flagged for those late returns.
  • INV-FLG-7: A neighbor flagged again while an earlier flag is still open on Neighbors gets a second Neighbor Flagged.
    • An earlier flag never stops a new one. Neighbors keeps one row for the neighbor, with the count and the latest date.
  • INV-FLG-9: Flagging a neighbor again for exactly the loans an earlier Neighbor Flagged already names succeeds and records nothing.
  • INV-FLG-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-3, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active, with late returns of loans L1 on 1 September, L2 on 20 September and L3 on 5 October, none named by an earlier flag. It is 5 October.
    • When: the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded.
  • Four counting late returns (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded naming all four.
  • A loan left out (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1, L2, L3 and L4
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with only L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." No event is recorded.
  • Below the threshold (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana has counting late returns L1 and L2 only
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1 and L2
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." No event is recorded.
  • A late return drops out of the window (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 1 June, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." The 1 June return is more than 90 days back. No event is recorded.
  • Window boundary (INV-FLG-2)
    • Given: Ana's late returns were on 8 July, 20 September and 5 October, none flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 on 5 October with all three loans
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded: 8 July is the 89th day before 5 October, so it still counts.
  • Flagged again on new late returns (INV-FLG-4, INV-FLG-7)
    • Given: Ana was flagged on 5 October for L1, L2 and L3, and the shed manager hasn't acted. Since then she returned L5, L6 and L7 late, on 20 October, 1 November and 15 November.
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L5, L6 and L7 on 15 November
    • Then: Neighbor Flagged is recorded again, naming L5, L6 and L7.
  • Used-up returns don't count again (INV-FLG-2, INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and returned L5 late since
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2, L3 and L5
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Only L5 counts. No event is recorded.
  • An old loan named alongside new ones (INV-FLG-4)
    • Given: Ana was flagged for L1, L2 and L3, and has since returned L5, L6 and L7 late
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L5, L6 and L7
    • Then: refused with late-returns-changed: "The late returns behind this flag have changed." L1 was used up by the earlier flag. No event is recorded.
  • The same flag arrives twice (INV-FLG-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Flagged was recorded for N1, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • When: Flag Neighbor for N1 with L1, L2 and L3 is issued again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, with 3 late returns from before her suspension that were never flagged
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "This neighbor is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Count reset by reinstatement (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana returned L1, L2 and L3 late, then was suspended and reinstated
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1 with L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: refused with below-threshold: "This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count." Returns from before her reinstatement don't count. No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-FLG-5)
    • Given: Ana's account was closed after she reached 3 counting late returns
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N1
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-FLG-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: Flag Neighbor is issued for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing; the Late Return Flagger logs it with the neighbor ID and moves on. No person sees these reasons. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. neighbor-not-found (INV-FLG-10).
  2. If a Neighbor Flagged for this neighbor already names exactly these loans, the command succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9).
  3. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-FLG-5).
  4. below-threshold (INV-FLG-2).
  5. late-returns-changed, if the loans given aren't exactly the neighbor's counting late returns (INV-FLG-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-FLG-10
account-closed This account is closed. INV-FLG-5
neighbor-suspended This neighbor is suspended. INV-FLG-5
below-threshold This neighbor has fewer than 3 late returns that count. INV-FLG-2
late-returns-changed The late returns behind this flag have changed. INV-FLG-4

neighbor-not-found, account-closed and neighbor-suspended mean the same conditions as in the neighbor commands; the sentences here fit a system log. A missing or malformed ID, or an empty loan list, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Flag Neighbor with the same loans succeeds and records nothing (INV-FLG-9). The flagger may act on the same neighbor twice before Neighbor Flagged lands; the second command is then a repeat.

late-returns-changed means the list moved on between the flagger's read and the command, for example a fourth late return landed. The flagger acts again on the list's updated entry, which gives the current set.

Requests at the same moment: Flag Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A suspension, reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed when a neighbor is flagged.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the Late Return Flagger issues Flag Neighbor. No person or screen does. It is an internal automation command, not on the REST API, so it has no sign-in guard.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Flagged links a neighbor to loans they returned late. It holds no name or email.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the list's freshness. The flagger acts as soon as the neighbor appears on Neighbors To Flag, shortly after the late return that crosses the threshold is recorded.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, neighborId, toolName, dueDate, returnedOn, late.
    • Neighbor Flagged (this slice): neighborId, lateReturns.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md and slices/return-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Read model this slice's processor reads: Neighbors To Flag (slices/neighbors-to-flag.md): each neighbor due a flag, with all their counting late returns.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and Neighbors To Flag. Suspend Neighbor is offered on Neighbors.

Open Questions

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v2: reworded to Neighbors (2026-11-01)

Slice: Suspend Neighbor

Intent

Let the shed manager suspend any active neighbor, so someone who keeps returning tools late stops borrowing until the shed manager reinstates them. Usually the neighbor has been flagged for late returns. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager issues Suspend Neighbor from the Neighbors screen, for any active neighbor, flagged or not. The usual case is a neighbor the system has flagged for late returns, whose flags and late returns the screen shows; it also covers a neighbor who closed their account while suspended and signed up again with a different email.

The system never suspends anyone: reaching the late-return threshold only flags a neighbor. (Version 1 drew this trigger from a separate Flagged Neighbors screen; v2 folds that screen into Neighbors.)

Command / Input

Command: Suspend Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to suspend. Must be a registered account (INV-SUS-10) that isn't closed (INV-SUS-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The flag and its late returns are usually the reason, and a suspension from the Neighbors screen needs none. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Neighbors @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Suspended → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (status suspended, the suspended date, the open flags cleared, Reinstate offered), My Account (status suspended), and Neighbors To Flag (a suspended neighbor is never flagged). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to refuse a suspended neighbor.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
suspendedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Reinstated lifts the suspension; a later suspension records a new Neighbor Suspended.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Suspended feeds Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

Suspension's effects are rules of the slices that refuse a suspended neighbor, each with its own reason the neighbor can see: a suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, including one set aside for them (INV-CHK-7, Check Out Tool), extend a loan (INV-EXT-7, Extend Loan), place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9, Place Hold) or change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email). They keep what they already have: their loans stay out and they can return them (INV-RET-7, Return Tool), and their holds keep their places and can be cancelled. A set-aside they can't collect expires at the end of its collect-by date, as any other (Expire Hold). While suspended they are never flagged (Flag Neighbor, INV-FLG-5). A suspension lasts until the shed manager reinstates the neighbor (Reinstate Neighbor); it never lifts by itself and is never permanent. The neighbor isn't emailed: they see the suspension on My Account and as the reason whenever something is refused. Neighbors and My Account own how a suspension is shown.

  • INV-SUS-1: Only the shed manager suspends a neighbor.
    • Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • INV-SUS-2: Only an active neighbor can be suspended.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be suspended, because closed is final.
    • Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended changes nothing (INV-SUS-9).
  • INV-SUS-9: Suspending a neighbor who is already suspended succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second suspension.
  • INV-SUS-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-SUS-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: suspending a flagged neighbor (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is active and shown flagged on Neighbors after three late returns within 90 days. She has the ladder on loan and a hold waiting on the cordless drill.
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 from Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her loan and her hold are untouched.
  • Suspending a neighbor who isn't flagged (INV-SUS-1, INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is active and not flagged
    • When: the shed manager suspends N2 from the Neighbors screen
    • Then: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2.
  • Suspending again after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and later reinstated, so she is active
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1
    • Then: a new Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1.
  • Already suspended (INV-SUS-9)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: the shed manager suspends N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A late copy after reinstatement (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: the shed manager suspended N1, and then reinstated her
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Suspend Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed account (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N3's account is closed
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-SUS-2)
    • Given: N4 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to suspend N4
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." Its status is closed, not suspended, so this isn't treated as a repeat. No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-SUS-1)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to suspend N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-SUS-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to suspend N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-SUS-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for suspending a neighbor arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the screen they acted from. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-SUS-11): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-SUS-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-SUS-10).
  4. If the neighbor's status is already suspended, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-SUS-9). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed, not the repeat.
  5. account-closed (INV-SUS-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-SUS-11
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can suspend neighbors. INV-SUS-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-SUS-10
account-closed This account is closed. INV-SUS-2

not-shed-manager, neighbor-not-found and account-closed mean the same conditions as in Add Tool, Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screens, which offer Suspend only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: suspension is a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is suspended) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a reinstatement suspends again.

Requests at the same moment: Suspend Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A reinstatement or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may suspend a neighbor (INV-SUS-1). Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Suspended links a neighbor to a suspension. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Registered matches slices/register-neighbor.md. Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor refuse a suspended neighbor; Reinstate Neighbor lifts the suspension.

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Reinstate Neighbor

Intent

Let the shed manager lift a neighbor's suspension, so the neighbor can borrow again with a clean late-return record.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Neighbors screen, for a neighbor shown there as suspended. A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time. (Version 1 drew this trigger from a separate Suspended Neighbors screen; v2 folds that screen into Neighbors.)

Command / Input

Command: Reinstate Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor to reinstate. Must be a registered account (INV-REI-8) that isn't closed (INV-REI-2).

There is no reason or note field: nothing is recorded about why. The command carries no "from" status: a late copy of an older request counts as a new request.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Neighbors @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Reinstated → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors (status active, the suspended date cleared, Suspend offered again), My Account (status active), and Neighbors To Flag (the late-return count starts again). Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor read it to know the suspension has lifted.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
reinstatedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. A later Neighbor Suspended suspends the neighbor again.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Reinstated feeds Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag, each specified in its own doc and eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

A reinstated neighbor is active again: they can check out tools, extend loans, place holds, collect set-aside tools and change their email, each under that slice's usual rules. A neighbor can be reinstated while they still have an overdue loan; the overdue loan goes on blocking checkouts and pickups until the tool is returned (INV-CHK-5, Check Out Tool). Holds they kept while suspended carry on from their place in the queue. Reinstatement starts the neighbor's late-return count again from zero: late returns from before it never count toward a later flag (INV-NTF-5, Neighbors To Flag; INV-FLG-5, Flag Neighbor). The neighbor isn't emailed; My Account shows them as active again. Neighbors and My Account own how a reinstatement is shown.

  • INV-REI-1: Only the shed manager reinstates a neighbor.
    • Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • INV-REI-2: Only a suspended neighbor can be reinstated.
    • A neighbor whose account is closed can't be reinstated, because closed is final, even if they were suspended when they closed it.
    • Reinstating a neighbor who is already active changes nothing (INV-REI-7).
  • INV-REI-7: Reinstating a neighbor who is already active succeeds and records nothing.
    • So a double submit, or a retry after a lost response, never records a second reinstatement.
  • INV-REI-8: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-REI-9: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REI-1, INV-REI-2)
    • Given: Ana (N1) is suspended, and shown so on Neighbors. She has two late returns within the last 90 days, a hold waiting at position 2 on the cordless drill, and an overdue ladder loan.
    • When: the shed manager reinstates N1 from Neighbors
    • Then: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1, with the time it was recorded. Nothing else is recorded: her hold and her loan are untouched.
  • Already active (INV-REI-7)
    • Given: N1 was reinstated and is active
    • When: the shed manager reinstates N1 again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • Never suspended (INV-REI-7)
    • Given: Ben (N2) has never been suspended
    • When: the shed manager asks to reinstate N2
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing is recorded.
  • A late copy after a new suspension (INV-REI-2)
    • Given: the shed manager reinstated N1, and later suspended her again
    • When: a delayed copy of the earlier Reinstate Neighbor request for N1 arrives
    • Then: it counts as a new request: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1 again.
  • Closed while suspended (INV-REI-2)
    • Given: N3 was suspended and then closed their account
    • When: the shed manager tries to reinstate N3
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager (INV-REI-1)
    • Given: N1 is suspended
    • When: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role asks to reinstate N1
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can reinstate neighbors." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-REI-8)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: the shed manager asks to reinstate N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-REI-9)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for reinstating a neighbor arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Neighbors screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-REI-9): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-REI-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-REI-8).
  4. If the neighbor's status is already active, the request succeeds and records nothing (INV-REI-7). Status is tested with closed first: an account closed while suspended has status closed, so it gets account-closed.
  5. account-closed (INV-REI-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-REI-9
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can reinstate neighbors. INV-REI-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-REI-8
account-closed This account is closed. INV-REI-2

The names mean the same conditions as in Suspend Neighbor. neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen, which offers Reinstate only on listed neighbors. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: reinstatement sets a state, and the command carries no "from" status. A request whose effect has already happened (the neighbor is active) succeeds and records nothing. A late copy of an older request that arrives after a new suspension reinstates again.

Requests at the same moment: Reinstate Neighbor is decided against the neighbor's events as already recorded, one at a time per neighbor. A suspension or closure landing at the same moment is decided in the same order: whichever is recorded first stands.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Nothing is emailed.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may reinstate a neighbor (INV-REI-1). Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Reinstated links a neighbor to a reinstatement. It holds no name, email or reason.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (this slice): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md and slices/suspend-neighbor.md. Close Account is specified in a slice not yet written in depth; it is checked against this key when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors, My Account and Neighbors To Flag. Check Out Tool, Extend Loan, Place Hold, Change Email and Flag Neighbor treat the neighbor as active again.

Open Questions

None.
